subtype: Approach: expects things to work because they should [Pitfall]
passage:
Ritwik had worked hard for three years: top marks in the lab, a project he was proud of, late nights before every submission. So when the company interview was fixed for Thursday morning, he did not open a single page about the company. Hard work always paid off, he told his roommate, so the interview would go well.
The train was delayed, and he walked in breathless with ten minutes to spare.
"What do you know about our product line?" the panel asked. Then: "How would you approach this case study?" He knew neither. He answered with stories about effort, and the panel nodded politely and wrote very little.

qa.q: Which day was the interview fixed for?
qa.a: The interview was fixed for Thursday morning.

qa.q: What did Ritwik expect about the interview, and why?
qa.a: Ritwik expected it to go well because hard work always paid off, and felt confident enough to skip any preparation.

qa.q: What could Ritwik have done in the days before the interview?
qa.a: Ritwik could have read about the company and practised a sample case study, since the panel asked about those exact things and general effort could not answer them.

qa.q: How might the panel see Ritwik's answers?
qa.a: The panel nodded politely and wrote very little, so they may have seen a hard-working person who had not prepared for their questions.

grounding: A student assumes that working hard in general means the interview will go well and does no preparation.

subtype: Approach: expects things to work because they should [Pitfall]
passage: Varun had topped his department and spent four years working late in the lab. When the campus interview call came from a big engineering firm, his friend Shankar asked, "Mock interview tonight?" Varun laughed. "I've worked harder than anyone. It'll go fine." He watched a film instead. The next morning, in the interview room in the Pune office, the first question was, "Tell us about a time you disagreed with a teammate." Varun blanked. Then, "Why this company?" He said something vague about growth. Then, "Explain your final project in two minutes for a non-engineer." He took eight and used jargon. The panel thanked him politely. Walking out, he realised hard work had never taught him how to answer these questions.

qa.q: What was the first interview question?
qa.a: "Tell us about a time you disagreed with a teammate."

qa.q: What was Varun feeling as he walked out?
qa.a: He felt shaken and deflated, realising his hard work hadn't prepared him for these questions.

qa.q: What other approach could Varun have taken?
qa.a: Accept Shankar's mock interview and practise common questions, so his real effort could come across clearly.

qa.q: How might Shankar feel hearing how it went?
qa.a: Shankar may feel sorry for Varun, and a little frustrated that his offer was brushed off.

grounding: A student assumes his hard work guarantees a good interview and does no preparation, and the specific questions catch him out.

subtype: Approach: expects things to work because they should [Pitfall]
passage:
"Kiran, the interview is tomorrow. Shouldn't you practise?"
"Kavitha, I've done three internships and I never miss a deadline. They'll see that."
"They'll only see it if you can say it."
"It'll work out. It always does if you work hard."
Next evening.
"So? How did it go?"
Kiran dropped onto the sofa. "They asked me to describe a failure and what I learned."
"And?"
"I said I don't really fail." He covered his face. "Then they asked why I wanted to work in banking operations specifically. I had no idea what to say. I just said I'm hardworking. Twice."
"Oh, Kiran."
"I thought effort would show on its own."
Kavitha sat beside him. "It does in the work. Interviews are a different skill."

qa.q: What did Kiran say when asked to describe a failure?
What was Kiran feeling when he covered his face?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and disappointed, realising effort alone hadn't answered their questions.

qa.q: What could Kiran do before his next interview?
qa.a: Practise answers to common questions, such as a failure and why this field, with Kavitha asking them.

qa.q: How does Kavitha see what happened?
qa.a: Kavitha is sympathetic but not surprised; she knew interviews are a different skill from the work itself.

grounding: A student assumes that working hard will make the interview go well and does no preparation, and it does not cover the questions.
